key_insight: The SSI detection AI model showed similar performance across age, gender, race, and skin color, but performance varied by geography.
clinical_relevance: This suggests the model may be broadly fair for several demographic groups, yet site-specific differences should be checked before clinical use.
method: Retrospective multicenter development and validation study using adult incision images submitted through the EHR within 30 days after surgery.
Compared AUROC across age, gender, geography, race, and skin color subgroups.
Used both internal training data and temporal validation to assess fairness over time.
evidence_signal: Training used 13,702 images from 4,274 patients and validation used 4,242 images from 1,353 patients; AUROC was 0.83-0.87 overall, with geography showing the only significant differences.
watch_item: The dataset was heavily skewed toward White and light-skin-tone patients, so fairness conclusions may be less certain for underrepresented groups and new hospital settings.
paper_title: Assessment of Fairness and Bias of an Image-based Surgical Site Infection Detection AI Model
